clue.text: Blase and far from satisfactory employee

parts.note: food or a performance that is off has gone bad or below par
a hand is a worker, as in a farmhand or deckhand

explanation.surface: A bored, poorly performing member of staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blase' at the start is the definition; the rest builds the word in two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe a casual, unconcerned manner that shows little interest.

clue.text: Old boy's restorative-there's a cryptic clue!

parts.note: OB is old boy, a former pupil of a school; the possessive adds S
a cure is a remedy that restores health

explanation.surface: A former pupil's remedy comes with a puzzling hint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there's a' and 'clue' are joining words around the definition 'cryptic', which plays on the puzzle itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mysterious or hard to understand is unclear, hidden in meaning.

clue.text: Lay it on thick so it's more even

definitions.meaning: smoother or more level, comparative of a word for level

explanation.definitionFit: Excessive praise is laying it on thick, and a level surface that is smoother is the comparative of plane.

clue.text: Designate a levy to be raised

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read upwards, so the toll word is turned round

parts.note: a toll is a charge or levy, as on a road

explanation.surface: Someone names a tax to be increased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be raised' turns TOLL into LLOT, which follows A.
explanation.definitionFit: To assign or set aside a share for someone is to earmark it.

clue.text: Many have a just claim, that's clear

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred, a large number
to own is to have or possess
a right is a just entitlement

explanation.surface: Lots of people have a fair entitlement, which is plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' stands for D, 500 in Roman numerals; 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something utter and unmistakable, such as a lie, is plain and obvious.

clue.text: Rebuilt Capitol-very up-to date

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together again in a new form, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A newly reconstructed Capitol is thoroughly modern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rebuilt' rearranges the seven letters of CAPITOL.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter of current interest, in the news now, is said to be highly current.

clue.text: Bound to draw from a newspaper leader

parts.note: to tap a barrel is to draw liquid from it
ED is short for editor, who heads a newspaper

explanation.surface: Obliged to take material from a newspaper's leading article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' suggests an editorial article, but it is the person who leads the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Something secured with adhesive strip is tied up or fastened.

clue.text: He'll bear the cost if tea's served in nicer surroundings

indicators.note: served in places the tea inside another word, as a drink is served in a cup
surroundings says the word for nicer forms the outside around the tea

parts.note: purer can mean cleaner or nicer
cha is a slang word for tea; the possessive adds S

explanation.surface: A customer pays more if tea is served somewhere pleasanter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served in ... surroundings' puts CHAS inside PURER, giving PUR-CHAS-ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A buyer is the one who pays the price for goods.

clue.text: Agree the artist is a monster!

parts.note: to chime with something is to agree with it
RA, Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: Someone agrees that the painter is a brute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link between the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this fire-breathing beast had a lion's head, goat's body and serpent's tail.

clue.text: Left at home to dine, note, as ruled

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
to eat is to dine
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Someone stays home to dine, noting as instructed.
explanation.definitionFit: Marked with lines, like paper with printed lines, describes something ruled.

clue.text: Winger points to permit

parts.note: S for south is a compass point
W for west is a second compass point
to allow something is to permit it

explanation.surface: A footballer on the wing gestures to give consent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests a footballer but means a bird; 'points' supplies two compass letters, S and W.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird is a creature with wings, so a crossword can call this small bird a winger.

clue.text: Some wine no-one sent back

parts.note: port is a fortified wine from Portugal

indicators.note: sent back tells us to read the letters for no-one in the opposite direction

parts.note: read as NO plus I, the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A drinker returns a glass of wine nobody wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns NO + I (one as a Roman numeral) into ION, which follows PORT.
explanation.definitionFit: A share or part of a whole is a quantity of it, as in some of the cake.

clue.text: Given no training, due to turn-around

indicators.note: the word around here means the preceding letters are moved round into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone lacks training because of a sudden change of direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn-around' looks like one word, but 'turn' is fodder and 'around' rearranges DUE TO TURN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has never had a tutor or teacher lacks formal schooling.

clue.text: Beast's expression of derision about aspiration

annotationWithheld.why: Beast's expression of derision about aspiration (5): H for aspiration, but no expression of derision giving the remaining Y, E, N, A with H inside could be found, and no scan or blog confirms the clue as printed
annotationWithheld.clue: Beast's expression of derision about aspiration

clue.text: Awesome Oriental lake

parts.note: E for east, the Orient
Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: An impressive lake in the Far East.
explanation.definitionFit: Here the word has its older sense of inspiring awe or dread, an uncanny feeling.

clue.text: FULLY OCCUPIED" written in large letters

definitions.meaning: a legal document can be written out in a large formal hand

explanation.definitionFit: Being absorbed means wholly busy, and a deed copied fair in a big clear hand has been put in that formal script.

clue.text: Stretches yarn that's become hard

parts.note: something that stretches gets bigger, it grows
a yarn is a story or tale

explanation.surface: A long story that has toughened up as it went on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yarn' looks like knitting wool but means a story; 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread left out goes stale, which means it turns dry and firm.

clue.text: Bully and harass, or go after work

indicators.note: go after places the harass and or pieces after the work piece in the answer

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work
to press someone is to harass or pressure them
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tyrant urged to harass people, or else chase after a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go after' puts PRESS and OR after OP; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant who rules harshly is someone who intimidates others.

clue.text: A flighty creature operating in erratic fashion

indicators.note: something done erratically is irregular and disordered, so the letters of the word before are jumbled

explanation.surface: An unreliable creature that operates unpredictably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in erratic fashion' rearranges OPERATING. An orange-tip is a common European butterfly.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a white butterfly whose male has orange wing tips, and butterflies fly.

clue.text: Shock at rogue's twist

indicators.note: twist means the letters given before it are wrung into a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A scoundrel's devious turn causes dismay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twist' rearranges AT ROGUE; the possessive S is not used.
explanation.definitionFit: Great anger or indignation is a strong reaction like being appalled.

clue.text: A woman's to take in the gambling stake

indicators.note: in places the catching word inside the stake word

parts.note: an ante is the stake put up in poker before play
to net is to catch or take, as with a fish

explanation.surface: A woman is to accept a bet in a card game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts NET inside ANTE, giving AN-NET-TE; the apostrophe S of 'woman's' means is.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a female first name, so it identifies one particular woman.

clue.text: Come round repeatedly about a dog

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A dog keeps coming back.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens again and again keeps returning.

clue.text: Money may be made by the small company in time

parts.note: CO is the short form of company
taken as written
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Cash may be generated by a small firm over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be made by the' links definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Coins in circulation are a form of currency.

clue.text: Redhead on the way out seems to back down

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here the first of Red

parts.note: an egress is an exit

explanation.surface: A red-haired person leaving appears to retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Redhead' looks like a person but splits as the head of 'Red'; 'on the' and 'seems to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To go back to an earlier, worse state is to retreat or retrogress.

clue.text: Colour, and leave the dance

parts.note: tan is a yellowish-brown colour
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Someone gets a suntan and then walks out of the dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link between the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a ballroom dance that originated in Argentina.

clue.text: Produce notes about sailboat drawing

indicators.note: about means the singing goes round the outside of the boat word

parts.note: to sing is to produce musical notes
a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: A musician makes notes about a sailing boat in a drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts KETCH inside SING, giving S-KETCH-ING.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a quick outline picture with a pencil is a form of art.

clue.text: The Spaniard one's possibly put right

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters can be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A Spanish gentleman may well be put right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges ONES (one's, without the apostrophe) and R follows; 'put' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Spanish form of address for a man, equivalent to mister.

clue.text: Associate with soft and rather stupid person

parts.note: a chum is a friend or associate
P is piano, the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: Someone mixes with a gentle, fairly dim individual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link between the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A fool or blockhead is an informal word for a silly person.

clue.text: Worker showing little heart is anxious

indicators.note: showing little of the following words means only a part of them is on display, letters inside them

explanation.surface: A labourer showing little courage is nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little heart' looks like a lack of courage, but 'showing little' points to letters hidden across heART IS ANxious.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled craftsman who works with their hands is a kind of labourer.

clue.text: Wise man holding America responsible for pre-packed food

indicators.note: holding means the wise man's word grips the country's letters inside it

parts.note: a sage is a wise man
USA, United States of America

explanation.surface: A wise man blames America for processed food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts USA inside SAGE; 'responsible for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Minced meat is filled into a skin casing, so it comes in a natural wrapper.

clue.text: English people joining the German reformer

parts.note: men are people
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: Englishmen join a German reformer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joining' is a link between the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who corrects and improves a text makes changes to it for the better.

clue.text: Keep back engineers and reporters

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
the press is a collective term for journalists

explanation.surface: Engineers and journalists are held back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link between the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain or hold down a feeling is to stop it showing.
